Irene / team — initial findings:

- Observed behavior: between 08:40–09:00 PST a single tenant in pool gpu-edu-03 started producing very large batches and sustained KV cache churn. This pushed per-worker memory footprint up and caused backpressure which cascaded to queueing. Our scheduler temporarily throttled other tenants to preserve OOM safety — that throttling explains the apparent reserved QPS shortfall.
- Evidence: snapshot from runtime metrics shows per-GPU queue depth spike + KV eviction rate 7x baseline (attaching short metrics export).

Short remediation actions I kicked off (live now):
1) Isolated the noisy workload and moved suspect jobs to a secondary sandbox pool to stop KV churn.
2) Increased worker parallelism for ClearWave's reserved slice (raised soft limit) and enabled their fallback routing to hosted variant (clearwave-hosted-v1) — traffic gradually shifting now.
3) Tuning: disabled the largest batch-path for the offending tenant, reducing memory pressure.

ETA: core queue depth should be below thresholds in ~45–90 minutes once routing completes and caches stabilize. I'll follow up with concrete metrics once steady.

Questions for leadership: do we grant immediate emergency burst (1.5–2x reserved) and apply a one-time credit for the service disruption? If yes, I need ops to flip the authorization flag.

Jonas
